comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom develops complex digital/mixed signal CMOS and analog III-V semiconductor devices, offering thousands of products for markets including AI networking, data centers, telecommunications, and factory automation.
comparisons.comparison: While AMD focuses on embedded computing and general-purpose accelerators (CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs), Broadcom (AVGO) discloses a semiconductor portfolio focused on digital/mixed-signal CMOS and analog III-V devices for AI networking and data center storage. AMD lists 'storage and networking' markets and 'Adaptive SoCs' which may include FPGA-based networking functions. Broadcom explicitly mentions 'enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking' and 'data center servers and storage systems' using its devices. Both companies serve the data center and networking infrastructure markets with custom silicon, though Broadcom's description is more specific to networking/storage semiconductor devices rather than the broader embedded/compute portfolio highlighted by AMD.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.

We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes ("STB"), broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose a diversified hardware portfolio extending beyond traditional CPUs to include specialized accelerators and processing units for diverse workloads. AMD specifically highlights its leadership in 'embedded computing' with APUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoCs that incorporate 'dedicated AI processing capabilities.' Similarly, Intel describes an 'xPU approach' delivering 'client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators' to meet diverse computing needs. Both companies emphasize a multi-architecture strategy involving FPGAs and GPUs alongside their core processors to address embedded and specific workload requirements.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
We also incorporate dedicated AI processing capabilities into our embedded portfolio.
Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

comparisons.peer_summary: NAND products are non-volatile, re-writeable storage devices used in SSDs for data centers, client PCs, consumer, and automotive markets, as well as in removable storage, managed NAND for mobile/embedded markets, and low-density NAND for automotive and industrial applications.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and Micron both serve the data center and storage markets, but with fundamentally different products. AMD incorporates its 'CPUs, APUs, FPGAs... used in... storage and networking' markets, providing the compute and processing logic for storage systems. Micron describes 'NAND products... used in SSDs for the data center, client PC... and automotive markets,' providing the memory storage component itself. Both companies identify the data center and automotive/industrial markets as key end markets, but AMD provides the processing architecture while Micron provides the non-volatile storage medium.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
NAND: NAND products are non-volatile, re-writeable semiconductor storage devices that provide high-capacity, low-cost storage with a variety of performance characteristics.
NAND is used in SSDs for the data center, client PC, consumer, and automotive markets and in removable storage markets.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hardware Foundation: GPUs, DPUs, and CPUs
comparisons.peer_summary: The platform is founded on GPUs for parallel workloads, expanded in fiscal year 2022 to include DPUs and in fiscal year 2024 to include CPUs, allowing optimization across the computing, networking, and storage stack.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and NVIDIA both describe their data center and compute platforms as comprehensive stacks that integrate multiple hardware types, including CPUs and GPUs, to optimize performance for parallel workloads. AMD states it delivers a full portfolio of 'CPUs, APUs, FPGAs... used in a variety of markets... including... storage and networking' with 'dedicated AI processing capabilities.' NVIDIA describes its platform as founded on 'GPUs' for parallel workloads, which expanded in fiscal year 2024 to include 'CPUs,' allowing optimization across the 'computing, networking and storage stack.' Both firms integrate CPUs and GPUs (or APUs equivalent) into a unified accelerated computing or platform strategy.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
We also incorporate dedicated AI processing capabilities into our embedded portfolio.
At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.
Beyond GPUs, our data center platform expanded to include DPUs in fiscal year 2022 and CPUs in fiscal year 2024.
We can optimize across the entire computing, networking and storage stack to deliver data center-scale computing solutions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm emphasize System-on-Chip (SoC) or heterogeneous computing architectures that integrate CPUs, GPUs, and dedicated AI accelerators (NPUs) to deliver high-performance computing. AMD mentions delivering 'CPUs, APUs... and Adaptive SoCs' with 'dedicated AI processing capabilities.' Qualcomm describes its 'System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance... computing.' Both companies explicitly integrate dedicated AI processing hardware into their SoC designs for performance and efficiency.

sentences.text: We are a leader in embedded computing, where we deliver high-performance and scalability across a full portfolio of CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, system on modules (SOMs) and Adaptive SoCs that are used in a variety of markets, including automotive, industrial, healthcare, storage and networking.
We also incorporate dedicated AI processing capabilities into our embedded portfolio.

We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.
